summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of titanium dioxide (TiO2) using two heteroleptic titanium precursors, Ti(OiPr)3(NiPr-Me-amd) and Ti(NMe2)2(OiPr)2, with ozone as the oxygen source. The process exhibits self-limiting growth behavior up to a maximum temperature of 325 °C. The growth rates are 0.3 Å/cycle and 0.9 Å/cycle for the two precursors at 325 °C, respectively. Both precursors deposit TiO2 in the anatase phase within the temperature range of 275−325 °C. High-temperature X-ray diffraction (HTXRD) studies reveal a thickness-dependent phase change from anatase to rutile at 875−975 °C for Ti(NMe2)2(OiPr)2. The films are of high purity and close to stoichiometric composition. In situ studies using quadrupole mass spectrometry (QMS) and quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) provide insights into the reaction mechanisms during the ALD process.
